subject: Mini-tutorial for printing tree structures with prt()

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Mini-tutorial for printing tree structures with prt()
parts:
Hi all,

Brief note:

R's tree structure is pretty non-intuitive, compared to the "a tree is a collection of node objects" structure that is taught in most phylogenetics courses and used in e.g. C++ software. It's done this way because R likes lists, and doesn't like objects.

I wrote the function prt() to help me figure it out:

Mini-tutorial for prt():
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#prt

This basic table structure is also used in the tables output by Biogeographic Stochastic Mapping, so understanding the results of prt() is the first step towards understanding the tables output by BSM.

Cheers!
Nick
